title: Grace notes that slide or hammer into the beat
description: Three acciaccaturas, each carrying the technique that joins it to its principal: a shift slide up string 1 from a grace F#4 (fret 2) to G#4 (fret 4), a hammer-on up string 4 from a grace D3 (open) to E3 (fret 2), and a legato slide up string 2 from a grace C4 (fret 1) to D4 (fret 3) — the commonest thing a guitar grace does, and the shape a Guitar Pro import produces (the No Surprises tutorial's bar 45). A fourth, full-size shift slide crosses the barline into bar 2, so the grace slides are read against the ordinary one. A grace takes no technique ordinal (it is not a beat a palm-mute run spans) but does record a site, so the line or slur starts at the small digit on tab and at the small notehead on the notation staff, clear of the grace's own shorter stem.
